name: The Thing
summary: A vast, Polyphemus-like sea creature that rose from the depths of a sunken chasm to embrace the great monolith, uttering strange measured sounds, and which may have later stalked the narrator to his door.
description:
The creature rose to the surface of the flooded chasm with only a slight churning of the water, revealing itself as vast, Polyphemus-like, and loathsome. It darted toward the great monolith like a stupendous monster of nightmare, flung its gigantic scaly arms about the stone, bowed its hideous head, and gave vent to certain measured sounds, apparently in a form of worship or communion with the ancient carved idol.

At the close of the narrator's account, an immense slippery body is heard lumbering against his door, suggesting the creature — or one like it — had tracked him to his refuge.

sources.quote: Then suddenly I saw it. With only a slight churning to mark its rise to the surface, the thing slid into view above the dark waters. Vast, Polyphemus-like, and loathsome, it darted like a stupendous monster of nightmares to the monolith, about which it flung its gigantic scaly arms, the while it bowed its hideous head and gave vent to certain measured sounds.
I hear a noise at the door, as of some immense slippery body lumbering against it.
